concepts.title: What is the Executive: Political and Permanent

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'What is the Executive: Political and Permanent' refers to.
questions.a: The executive is the organ that implements laws and runs the administration day to day. It has two layers: the political executive -- ministers who head departments and answer to the people through elections -- and the permanent executive or civil services, career officers who provide expertise and continuity beneath the ministers.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'What is the Executive: Political and Permanent'.
questions.a: Ministers decide, civil servants execute -- one gives direction and accountability, the other expertise and stability.

questions.q: Under which section is 'What is the Executive: Political and Permanent' taught, and from which source text?

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Parliamentary and Presidential Executives Compared' refers to.
questions.a: In a parliamentary form the legislature chooses and can dismiss the executive: the Prime Minister heads a council of ministers responsible to the Lok Sabha, and the head of state acts largely on advice. In a presidential form the people elect the President directly or nearly so, who appoints ministers not answerable to the legislature -- power is separated rather than fused.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Parliamentary and Presidential Executives Compared'.
questions.a: Fusion with responsibility, or separation with fixed tenure -- the two great designs of executive power.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Parliamentary and Presidential Executives Compared' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 1.2 (source: keps204.txt lines 110-230 (parliamentary executive, presidential executive, prime minister and president, collective responsibility, comparison of the two systems))

concepts.title: Prime Minister and Council of Ministers

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Prime Minister and Council of Ministers' refers to.
questions.a: The Prime Minister is the real head of government: he recommends ministers, allocates and reshuffles portfolios, chairs the cabinet, and coordinates all policy. The Council of Ministers works under collective responsibility -- sink or swim together with the government -- and individual responsibility for each department.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Prime Minister and Council of Ministers'.
questions.a: First among equals who is actually first -- the PM steers the cabinet and the cabinet answers to the house.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Prime Minister and Council of Ministers' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: President of India: Election, Powers and Discretion

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'President of India: Election, Powers and Discretion' refers to.
questions.a: The President is the constitutional head of state, elected indirectly by an electoral college of MPs and MLAs. Formally every action is taken in the President's name, but normally on the aid and advice of the council of ministers; however, the office retains discretionary moments -- appointing a Prime Minister in a hung house, or returning advice once for reconsideration.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'President of India: Election, Powers and Discretion'.
questions.a: A head of state who must normally obey ministers, but who keeps judgement for the rare hung-house and reconsideration moments.
